questions.question_text: Where is your AI risk management policy kept, and how do the people it applies to (staff, developers, vendors' account owners) come to know it and any changes to it, for example through onboarding, training, acknowledgement or announcements?
How do your AI rules apply to AI that others built or sold to you, as well as AI you run yourself, so that it meets your existing legal obligations and risk controls? Who checks this?

What do your procedures require to happen before an AI system goes live and while it is in use (testing and validation, legal and risk review, ongoing monitoring), and what record shows these steps were followed for a recent AI system?
How do your AI policies and procedures address qualities such as safety, security, fairness, explainability and privacy for your AI systems, and where can we see this applied to a recent AI system?
How do your rules for building and training your own models set standards for data quality and model training? Where can we see them applied to your latest model?
In the 'AI systems' sheet, list each AI system your organisation uses or builds, with what it involves and the worst realistic outcome if it gets things wrong.
How does a new or changed AI system get added to your AI system inventory, and who is responsible for that?
How does an AI system's criticality decide how much goes into its inventory entry — which details are recorded and how often it is reviewed — and where is that shown?

Where are your rules for using third-party AI (models, AI services and the data they rely on) kept, and how do the people they apply to come to know them and any changes, for example through onboarding, training or announcements?

Before your organisation starts using a third-party AI system or data source, how is it checked for what it does, what it was trained on and its known limits, for example through vendor documentation and your own testing? Who signs off?

How do you check that third-party AI and the data it was built on do not infringe someone else's intellectual property or other rights, for example through contract terms or licence reviews? Where is the outcome recorded?
How are your rules for third-party AI reviewed and updated, for example after a vendor change, an incident or a new law? Who owns that review?
How do you choose, check and keep watching the existing model your own model is built on, for example its source, licence and known weaknesses? Who owns this?
